changed_views: Vinci's account makes deployment and validation architecture more important to assess than the physics-foundation-model label: private customer inputs still enter at runtime, and existing thermal/thermo-mechanical coverage should be separated from broader expansion plans.

Figma and Melius illustrate two compatible ways for creative applications to retain a role in agent workflows: integrate agents with native editable context, and expose tools to external agents. The interviews do not yet establish which captures more revenue or retention.

General Medicine provides concrete evidence for fulfillment infrastructure as an AI application opportunity, but pharmacy-network breadth is not evidence of universal checkout, autonomous care or measured health improvement.
follow_ups: Seek Vinci customer-confirmed error/convergence benchmarks, deployment labor and time-to-market improvements on specified package geometries; distinguish existing thermo-mechanical support from future electromagnetic coverage.

Track Figma's design-system adherence, edit/rework rates and incremental paid usage after general availability; request the comparator, sample and grading protocol behind its roughly 60%+ evaluation-win claim.
Track General Medicine pharmacy pay-ahead eligibility, completed transactions and repeat use separately from the price-comparison footprint and registered customer count.
Ask Melius for paid customer counts and the fraction of paid usage through external agents, then verify timeline-editor and Adobe-plugin release dates and contribution margins.
Verify Mistral's actual weight publication, license and moderation configuration at the end of October; reconcile 49B versus 52B active parameters and run comparable workload evaluations.

signals.claim: Vinci's CEO says its semiconductor simulation model needs no customer-specific training and runs on premises without forward-deployed engineers; customer geometry and material data are still required at runtime.
signals.evidence: Kabaria says sales start with a VP's time-to-market and performance constraints, particularly thermal problems in HBM, GPUs and TPUs (02:23:43–02:24:43). He describes commercial deployment inside the customer's firewall with zero forward-deployed engineers (02:25:34, 02:26:09), and physics-based pretraining that avoids learning customers' proprietary designs (02:27:25–02:28:04). Vinci's [February product release](https://www.getvinci.ai/news/vinci-ships-production-grade-thermo-mechanical-simulation-at-manufacturing-scale/) supports the deployment claim and shows thermo-mechanical simulation was already shipping. Its [DAC account](https://www.getvinci.ai/blog/dac-2026-panel-what-breaks-validates-automates/) clarifies that private material inputs are supplied at runtime and that the system does not cover all physics at all scales. The useful proposition is a repeatable deployment that preserves IP; independent customer accuracy, deployment effort and economic outcomes are not established here. His 10–100× training-data expansion over coming quarters and electromagnetic expansion are forecasts (02:28:04), not proof of universal hardware autonomy. Nvidia, Micron, TSMC and Samsung are examples of protected designs, not identified customers.

signals.claim: Field positions Figma's generally available design agent around native canvas operations and design-system context, combining Figma's own models with frontier models rather than relying on one-shot generation.
signals.evidence: Field describes using both first-party and frontier models (02:01:15–02:01:29), improving context across files and design systems (02:01:33–02:01:50), and teaching models how to operate Figma so users can keep editing the result (02:06:45–02:07:33). Figma's [October 6 release](https://www.figma.com/blog/3-ways-product-designers-use-the-figma-agent/) confirms this is the exit from beta, adding library-owner Markdown guidelines automatically supplied to the agent, cross-product context retrieval, and the ability to follow collaborators' agents. Its [design-system workflow guide](https://www.figma.com/blog/figma-agent-and-design-systems/) describes auditing and replacing components and tokens. This provides a concrete mechanism for an incumbent editor to retain value as generation improves: use the organization's existing editable structure and rules. Neither Field's faster/higher-quality description nor the release establishes a general task-success or productivity rate; the release's roughly 60%+ human-graded evaluation wins lack enough comparator and sample detail to treat as either.

signals.claim: TJ Parker says General Medicine is building the pricing, records and fulfillment infrastructure that turns AI health advice into a purchase or appointment; its pharmacy comparison reach should not be confused with universal prepaid checkout.
signals.evidence: Parker says signup retrieves an average 11 years of records (01:25:08), combines healthcare pricing data with insurance/cash comparisons (01:25:30), and offers a pharmacy shopping experience across 50,000 locations (01:26:06). The [October 6 company release](https://generalmedicine.co/resources/general-medicine-raises-120-million-to-build-the-healthcare-store) corroborates the average record span and describes a common catalog that reconciles differently named services, with licensed clinicians determining appropriate care when review is required. The [storefront](https://generalmedicine.co/) advertises price comparison at 50,000+ pharmacies, but the [October 5 pharmacy documentation](https://generalmedicine.co/resources/compare-medication-prices-before-you-order-and-pay-ahead-for-easy-pickup) limits pay-ahead to eligible retail pharmacies using the uninsured/card route, excluding mail order. Parker's future agent and LLM shopping distribution (01:30:38–01:31:08) is a strategy, not evidence of deployed autonomous clinical decisions. The incremental business evidence is the transaction layer beyond advice; no conversion, repeat-use, margin or clinical-outcome data are provided in the interview.

signals.claim: Melius co-founder Joowon Kim says most customers already use its creative tools through Claude/ChatGPT plugins and MCP, making external agents an observed distribution channel; parts of the editing suite remain forthcoming.
signals.evidence: Kim says most customers use Claude and ChatGPT plugins with Melius MCP (01:37:08–01:37:58), describes a business open to off-platform usage (01:38:28–01:39:25), and gives a customer workflow that feeds scripts, transcripts and key frames from trending ads into Melius via a recurring Claude automation (01:40:12–01:40:37). His [October 6 announcement](https://www.melius.com/blog/melius-seed-and-series-a) confirms $25 million in total funding and marks the canvas, asset manager, and MCP/API/CLI as live, but the agentic timeline editor and Elements as coming soon. Proposed Premiere/After Effects plugins are also future work in the interview. This is concrete founder-reported use of agents as a product interface, without a disclosed customer denominator, paid usage, retention or acquisition-cost comparison. The claim that a customer exceeds $5 billion ARR describes that customer's scale, not Melius revenue; he does not establish a proprietary model-training plan when asked about inference economics.

signals.claim: Mistral Large 4 launches as a public API preview with open weights promised by the end of October; the episode's broad open-model ranking and parameter count need qualification.
signals.evidence: The hosts relay Mistral's launch claims of roughly one trillion total parameters, 49 billion active, European infrastructure, immediate API access and end-of-October weights (00:50:15–00:51:02). The [official announcement](https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4/) confirms preview access and the future weight release, while the [October 6 changelog](https://docs.mistral.ai/resources/changelogs) still says weights are coming soon. There is an unresolved documentation discrepancy: the announcement uses 1T/49B, while the [model page](https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-large) lists 1.05T/52B plus a 1.6B vision encoder. The hosts themselves dispute global leadership and distinguish regional availability from benchmark leadership (00:53:20–00:53:38). This adds a European-hosted candidate for workload evaluation, not an already downloadable model or verified overall frontier leader. Their speculation that the eventual weights will be cyber-nerfed is not a confirmed release policy.

summary: Hardik Kabaria describes Vinci's approach to semiconductor simulation: a physics-trained model deployed inside customer firewalls, without customer-specific training or forward-deployed engineers. Dylan Field explains Figma's move from agent beta to general availability around editable canvas work and design-system context. TJ Parker and Joowon Kim provide concrete examples of healthcare fulfillment and creative production becoming tools for agents; Mistral's new model is an API preview with weights still promised for later in October.
why_it_matters: The strongest evidence concerns what makes specialized AI useful inside an existing workflow: private runtime inputs and physical validation at Vinci, native components and design rules at Figma, transaction infrastructure at General Medicine, and external-agent distribution at Melius. These are specific product and deployment choices, while broad productivity, autonomous-operation, and model-leadership claims remain less well established.
